name: Newfoundland Coast + Gros Morne

dates.why: Aug 31-Sep 13 keeps Newfoundland in early September shoulder season: enough daylight, fewer peak crowds, and still-good odds for coastal hiking, boats, and village restaurants.

exchangeRateNote: Canadian-dollar lodging, food, ferry, and activity estimates use planning conversions and should be re-priced before booking.
positioning: A slower, wilder Atlantic Canada route: St. John's color and food, puffins and lighthouses, Trinity/Bonavista village coast, Twillingate and Fogo Island, then a Gros Morne finale with Tablelands and Western Brook Pond.
routeLabel: St. John's -> Avalon -> Trinity/Bonavista -> Twillingate -> Fogo -> Gros Morne -> Deer Lake
routeRationale: The route starts with three nights in St. John's so the first days have city services, stroller walks, good food, and easy weather backups before the long cross-island drives.
Bonavista/Trinity is the first rural base because it concentrates Skerwink Trail, Elliston puffins, Bonavista lighthouse, Port Rexton food, and heritage villages with short local drives.
Twillingate and Fogo are kept as two compact northern-island bases: high scenic payoff, ferry logistics, and one controlled splurge window without making Fogo Island Inn the default.
Gros Morne is saved for the finale because Tablelands, Woody Point, Norris Point, and Western Brook Pond are the most mountain-like Newfoundland moments and pair well with a Deer Lake departure.
The longest drives are broken by Terra Nova, Gander, Grand Falls-Windsor, or Deer Lake so the plan works around a one-year-old rather than assuming heroic car-seat tolerance.

visualStory.title: A city of color at the edge of the Atlantic
visualStory.copy: St. John's and Quidi Vidi make the trip feel alive before the road trip starts: bright houses, old harbor lanes, sea cliffs, and excellent food within short baby-friendly hops.
visualStory.alt: Bright Jellybean Row houses in St. John's.

visualStory.title: Lighthouses, puffins, and open water
visualStory.copy: Cape Spear and Witless Bay add the first wild-ocean day, with the boat kept optional so weather and baby rhythm stay in charge.
visualStory.alt: Atlantic puffins on Gull Island near Witless Bay.

visualStory.title: Trinity, Skerwink, and Bonavista cliffs
visualStory.copy: The Bonavista Peninsula is the sweet spot: sea stacks, painted harbor towns, lighthouses, puffin cliffs, and food-forward inns without changing beds every night.
visualStory.alt: Sea stacks along the Port Rexton coast.

visualStory.title: Twillingate and Fogo feel remote in the best way
visualStory.copy: This is the atmospheric middle of the trip: ferry timing, fishing villages, fog, art, and the option to turn one or two nights into a design-led splurge.
visualStory.alt: Fogo Island Inn on the rocky Newfoundland coast.

visualStory.title: Gros Morne is the big scenic payoff
visualStory.copy: The route ends with the island's most dramatic landscape: Tablelands, Bonne Bay, rocky lighthouses, and Western Brook Pond's fjord-like cliffs.
visualStory.alt: Western Brook Pond in Gros Morne National Park.

premiumStayStrategy.name: Monastery Hotel + Spa
premiumStayStrategy.cardAlt: Spa treatment imagery at Monastery Hotel + Spa.
premiumStayStrategy.priceDisplay: From about CAD $400/night for spa-package style stays
premiumStayStrategy.priceNote: Public package pricing shows a one-night King Jacuzzi Suite stay package from CAD $400; ordinary room-only rates should be re-quoted for Aug 31-Sep 3, 2026.
premiumStayStrategy.vibe: The clearest St. John's spa reset: massage/spa services in a quieter historic property, useful after the flight before the rural route starts.
premiumStayStrategy.story: Use Monastery when the first nights should feel like recovery, not just arrival logistics. It is the Newfoundland answer to the resort/spa note in the brief: land, sleep, take turns with a treatment, then begin the road trip calmer.
premiumStayStrategy.useFor: Swap for Blue on Water if the first two nights should feel restorative instead of just practical.
premiumStayStrategy.budgetEffect: Moderate premium; likely worth it for 2-3 arrival nights if spa access matters.
premiumStayStrategy.babyNote: Best as parent turn-taking during nap windows; request crib and confirm room layout.
premiumStayStrategy.bookingNote: Confirm whether the package rate applies to your dates and whether spa appointments can be reserved before arrival.
premiumStayStrategy.logistics: Works best as an arrival decompression base. Keep St. John's sightseeing short and let spa appointments sit around naps.
highlights: A real spa reset at the start of the route.
Short drives to Signal Hill, Quidi Vidi, and Cape Spear.
More restorative than a purely practical downtown room.

premiumStayStrategy.name: Alt Hotel St. John's
premiumStayStrategy.priceDisplay: Recent public snapshot around USD $277/night incl. taxes/fees
premiumStayStrategy.priceNote: OTA snapshot pricing varies by date and room type; use the official hotel site or preferred booking channel for Aug 31-Sep 3, 2026.
premiumStayStrategy.vibe: Modern harborfront boutique feel rather than resort/spa: easy walking, big water views, and less old-inn charm.
premiumStayStrategy.story: Alt is the clean, stylish, harborfront version of St. John's. It does not solve the spa wish the way Monastery does, but it makes the city base feel contemporary and easy.
premiumStayStrategy.useFor: Use if you want the city base to feel crisp, stylish, and low-friction.
premiumStayStrategy.budgetEffect: Usually a manageable premium over simpler downtown rooms.
premiumStayStrategy.babyNote: Strong convenience play: downtown walks, easy stroller outings, and straightforward hotel logistics.
premiumStayStrategy.bookingNote: Ask for crib availability, parking details, and a room category with enough floor space for baby gear.
premiumStayStrategy.logistics: Best when you want St. John's to be walkable and polished, with restaurants and harbor strolls close by.
highlights: Easy stroller access to downtown St. John's.
Less old-world romance, more polished convenience.

premiumStayStrategy.name: Fisher's Loft Inn
premiumStayStrategy.cardAlt: Guest room at Fisher's Loft Inn.
premiumStayStrategy.priceNote: Use as a planning range for room/cottage categories; exact 2026 availability and tax-inclusive pricing should be confirmed directly.
premiumStayStrategy.vibe: Not a spa resort, but very much the refined countryside-inn version: views, gardens, good food, and an intimate Newfoundland village-coast feel.
premiumStayStrategy.story: Fisher's Loft is the reason to linger around Port Rexton instead of making Bonavista a drive-through. It is the family-run, food-and-view inn that gives the middle of the trip a romantic countryside base.
premiumStayStrategy.useFor: Keep as the default nice stay for Trinity/Bonavista; this is the base where charm matters more than formal luxury.
premiumStayStrategy.budgetEffect: Worth preserving in the nice version; cottages/suites may push the base cost upward.
premiumStayStrategy.babyNote: Ask for crib, kitchenette/fridge options, and the easiest room-to-parking setup.
premiumStayStrategy.bookingNote: Book early and ask which room/cottage category works best with a crib and stroller gear.
premiumStayStrategy.logistics: Use this as a 3-night base for Skerwink, Trinity, Bonavista, Elliston, Port Rexton Brewing, and low-transit inn afternoons.
highlights: The refined village-inn anchor of the route.
Best base for Skerwink and Trinity.
Food-forward without being a formal resort.

premiumStayStrategy.name: Fogo Island Inn
premiumStayStrategy.cardAlt: Fogo Island Inn exterior and coastline.
premiumStayStrategy.priceDisplay: Public estimates often start around CAD $2,875+/night
premiumStayStrategy.priceNote: Fogo's official rate page emphasizes inclusions and direct inquiry; exact nightly rates for your dates should be confirmed with the inn. Treat this as the budget-changing centerpiece.
premiumStayStrategy.vibe: The true destination-resort moment of the whole trip: architecture, remote coast, serious food, cultural programming, and a design-hotel sense of occasion.
premiumStayStrategy.story: This is the stay that can sell the whole Newfoundland idea by itself. If the trip should have a world-class resort moment, make Fogo Island Inn the intentional two-night centerpiece and simplify spending elsewhere.
premiumStayStrategy.useFor: Make this the deliberate 2-night splurge if the trip should have a world-class stay.
premiumStayStrategy.budgetEffect: Major premium; this can add several thousand dollars versus a cottage/inn. Treat as the luxury version's centerpiece.
premiumStayStrategy.babyNote: Confirm child policy, crib, meal pacing, and whether the experience still feels relaxed with a one-year-old.
premiumStayStrategy.bookingNote: Contact the inn directly for exact dates, inclusions, dining, child policy, crib, and transfer/ferry advice.
premiumStayStrategy.logistics: Only do this if you are happy letting the stay itself be the activity: coast, design, food, cultural programming, and quiet.
highlights: The strongest resort-design moment in Newfoundland.
Best used as a two-night splurge, not a casual add-on.

dailyItinerary.title: Fly ATL to St. John's

gallery.alt: Bright Jellybean Row houses in St. John's.
gallery.caption: Arrive into color

dailyItinerary.overnight: Blue on Water / downtown St. John's
dailyItinerary.transport: Fly ATL to YYT on Air Canada or best one-stop routing via Toronto; taxi or short rental-car pickup to downtown.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Land, check in, stretch legs around Water Street and the harbor if arrival energy allows.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If delayed, skip everything except hotel check-in, simple food, and sleep.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Airport meals, then simple downtown dinner or room snacks.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Travel day: stroller in airports, carrier for boarding, no sightseeing pressure.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Price open-jaw flights into YYT and home from YDF, then book refundable downtown lodging.
dailyItinerary.why: St. John's gives the trip a colorful, serviced landing pad before the rural road trip begins.
moments: Wake up already downtown instead of adding a first-night drive.
Use city groceries and pharmacies before smaller villages.
Let the first evening be deliberately small.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Day 1 carries the full two-adult flight budget; return flight is counted here.

dailyItinerary.title: Signal Hill, Quidi Vidi, and city recovery
dailyItinerary.overnight: Blue on Water / downtown St. John's
dailyItinerary.transport: Short city driving or taxi loops; avoid parking stress if weather is rough.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Signal Hill viewpoints and Cabot Tower area, then Quidi Vidi village for a gentle harbor-and-cafe wander.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: The Rooms museum, Bannerman Park, or a nap-heavy downtown cafe day.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Breakfast downtown, lunch around Quidi Vidi or Rocket Bakery-style casual food, early dinner at Terre or Mallard Cottage if reservations work.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Stroller for downtown; carrier for Signal Hill steps and uneven paths.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Reserve one early dinner if choosing Mallard Cottage or Terre.
dailyItinerary.why: Signal Hill and Quidi Vidi make the place legible immediately: harbor, cliffs, painted houses, and old fishing-village texture without a long drive.
moments: Cabot Tower and the Narrows view.
Quidi Vidi harbor with an easy snack stop.
Nap back downtown before dinner.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Mostly food and local transport; no major paid activity required.

dailyItinerary.title: Cape Spear and Witless Bay decision day

gallery.alt: Cape Spear lighthouse near the Atlantic.
gallery.caption: Cape Spear edge-of-continent moment

dailyItinerary.overnight: Blue on Water / downtown St. John's
dailyItinerary.transport: Cape Spear is about 25 minutes from downtown; Witless Bay boat docks are about 35-45 minutes south of St. John's.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Cape Spear lighthouse and ocean viewpoints, with an optional short Witless Bay puffin/whale boat only if seas and baby temperament are good.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Skip the boat and do Petty Harbour, Bowring Park, and a calm late lunch instead.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Breakfast downtown, lunch near Petty Harbour or Bay Bulls, easy St. John's dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier at Cape Spear; boat is optional and should be skipped in wind, rain, or rough seas.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Ask the boat operator about infants, life jackets, sea conditions, and cancellation policy before paying.
dailyItinerary.why: This is the closest big-ocean drama to St. John's, with a flexible puffin/whale layer if conditions are kind.
moments: Stand at Cape Spear's eastern-edge viewpoints.
Decide on the boat based on weather, not sunk cost.
Keep bedtime protected before the first transfer day.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Activity cost assumes two adult boat tickets; it drops near zero if you choose the land-only version.

dailyItinerary.title: Drive to Port Rexton via Terra Nova

gallery.caption: Terra Nova break in the drive
First glimpse of the Port Rexton coast

dailyItinerary.transport: St. John's to Port Rexton is about 3.5 hours direct; break it with Terra Nova viewpoints or a short boardwalk.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Transfer day with a Terra Nova National Park leg-stretch, then check into Port Rexton/Trinity country.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If the baby hates the car, skip Terra Nova and go straight to the inn.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Breakfast in St. John's, picnic/grocery lunch en route, dinner at Fisher's Loft or Port Rexton Brewing food-truck style if operating.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Two driving blocks around nap; use Terra Nova only as a flexible reset.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Reserve Fisher's Loft or a cottage early; Port Rexton options are limited.
dailyItinerary.why: This moves from city Newfoundland to the quieter coves, trails, and food villages that make the island feel special.
moments: A national-park stop without making the day a hike day.
Arrive before dinner instead of after dark.
Settle into a three-night base.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transport includes rental-car allocation and fuel for the first longer drive.

dailyItinerary.title: Skerwink Trail and Trinity

gallery.alt: Sea stacks on the Port Rexton coast.
gallery.caption: The Skerwink-style payoff

gallery.alt: A sea stack in Robinhood Bay near Port Rexton.
gallery.caption: Carrier-friendly viewpoint energy

dailyItinerary.transport: Local drives around Port Rexton and Trinity, usually under 15 minutes per hop.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Do the baby-adjusted version of Skerwink Trail: viewpoints and a short carrier walk instead of committing to the full loop, then Trinity village.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If wet or windy, make it a Trinity heritage buildings, cafe, and inn-rest day.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Inn breakfast, lunch in Trinity or Port Rexton, Fisher's Loft dinner if available.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier day; cliff paths are not stroller terrain and require conservative turnaround points.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Ask the inn for current trail conditions and reserve dinner.
dailyItinerary.why: Skerwink is one of the strongest short-coast experiences in Newfoundland, but the plan uses it as a flexible viewpoint walk with a one-year-old.
moments: Sea stacks and cliff views without forcing the full loop.
Trinity's painted houses and harbor.
A calm inn dinner after an outdoor morning.
dailyItinerary.costNote: No paid activity needed; the value is in the trail and village.

dailyItinerary.title: Bonavista, Elliston puffins, and lighthouse coast

gallery.alt: Atlantic puffins on a grassy island.
gallery.caption: The birdlife layer

dailyItinerary.transport: Port Rexton to Bonavista/Elliston loop, about 1.5-2 hours total driving.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Cape Bonavista Lighthouse, Dungeon Provincial Park viewpoints, and Elliston puffin viewing from a respectful distance.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If fogged in, shorten to Bonavista town, cafes, and Ryan Premises/indoor heritage stops.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Breakfast at base, lunch in Bonavista, relaxed Port Rexton/Trinity dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier for puffin/cliff viewpoints; stay well back from edges and nesting areas.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Check puffin season realities before building the day around sightings; early September may be late.
dailyItinerary.why: Bonavista adds the iconic lighthouse-and-puffin layer that makes this route more than pretty driving.
moments: Cape Bonavista lighthouse in coastal wind.
Elliston puffin viewpoint if birds are still around.
Dungeon sea arch stop if the weather is clear.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Small museum/heritage fees only; puffin viewing itself is low-cost.

dailyItinerary.title: To Twillingate and Iceberg Alley
dailyItinerary.transport: Port Rexton to Twillingate is about 3.5-4 hours with a Gander or Boyd's Cove break.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Transfer to Twillingate, then an easy harbor walk or Long Point sunset if everyone has energy.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Go straight to the hotel and save Long Point for tomorrow.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Picnic/grocery lunch en route, early dinner at the inn or a Twillingate seafood/pub option.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Longer car day; plan one real stop and do not add sightseeing until after check-in.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Book Twillingate lodging with cancellation flexibility because weather can affect boat plans.
dailyItinerary.why: Twillingate gives a distinct northern coastal mood and a practical staging point before the Fogo ferry.
moments: Break the drive before the baby melts down.
Arrive with time for a harbor stroll.
Keep dinner simple.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transport reflects fuel and rental allocation for the cross-island leg.

dailyItinerary.title: Twillingate lighthouse and boat option
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Long Point Lighthouse, coastal viewpoints, and an optional short boat tour if sea state and infant policy are favorable.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Durrell Museum, cafes, Split Rock viewpoint, or a hotel-nap day if the weather turns.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Breakfast at lodging, seafood lunch or picnic, dinner in Twillingate.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier for viewpoints; boat is a weather-dependent bonus, not the spine of the day.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Call the boat operator about infants and same-day conditions before reserving.
dailyItinerary.why: This day gives Twillingate its due while keeping the family plan nimble around wind, rain, and nap timing.
moments: Long Point Lighthouse views.
Boat only if conditions look kind.
A low-transit afternoon before ferry logistics.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Activity cost assumes two adult boat tickets; land-only version is much cheaper.

dailyItinerary.title: Fogo Island ferry and Tilting

gallery.caption: Ferry day starts from the north coast

dailyItinerary.transport: Drive to Farewell, take the ferry to Fogo Island, then continue to Tilting/Joe Batt's Arm area.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Make the ferry the adventure, then explore Tilting, Joe Batt's Arm, and simple coastal boardwalks after check-in.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If ferry/weather timing slips, keep the day to transfer, groceries, and a short harbor walk.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Breakfast in Twillingate, ferry snacks/picnic lunch, cottage dinner or inn restaurant if booked.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Treat ferry waits as part of the schedule; pack layers, snacks, and a car-seat-friendly nap plan.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Confirm ferry schedule, lodging check-in, crib, and dining before leaving Twillingate.
dailyItinerary.why: Fogo is the route's artful, remote-feeling splurge: ferry rhythm, stark coast, fishing outports, and architecture that feels unlike the mainland island.
moments: Ferry crossing to Fogo.
Tilting's lanes and fishing-stage scenery.
A quiet cottage or inn evening.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Default assumes a cottage or modest inn. Fogo Island Inn can add several thousand dollars and should be a deliberate one- or two-night upgrade.

dailyItinerary.title: Fogo slow day, studios, and barrens

gallery.alt: Fogo Island Inn on rocky coast.
gallery.caption: Fogo Island Inn

dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Fogo Head or Brimstone Head viewpoints in a baby-short version, artist-studio architecture viewing, and a slow village lunch.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If it is windy or wet, make it a driving loop, cafes, craft shops, and nap-heavy indoor day.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Cottage breakfast, lunch near Joe Batt's Arm/Fogo, special dinner if staying at or near the inn.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier for boardwalks and viewpoints; skip exposed climbs if wind is high.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Prebook any Fogo Island Inn dining or community-hosted experience well ahead.
dailyItinerary.why: This is the quietest, strangest, most design-forward day of the trip: not many scheduled activities, just a place with a strong point of view.
moments: Fogo Island Inn exterior and coast views.
Short, safe viewpoint walk.
Unhurried village time.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Food is higher here because island dining and supply logistics can be expensive.

dailyItinerary.title: Drive to Gros Morne

gallery.alt: Western Brook Pond in Gros Morne.
gallery.caption: The west-coast reward ahead

dailyItinerary.transport: Fogo ferry back to Farewell, then drive west toward Gros Morne; about 5-6 hours of movement plus ferry timing.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: A pure transfer day with a Gander or Grand Falls-Windsor break, ending in Norris Point/Rocky Harbour.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If ferry timing makes the day too long, overnight around Gander and shorten Gros Morne by one night.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Simple ferry-day breakfast, road lunch, early dinner near Norris Point or Rocky Harbour.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Hardest logistics day: two nap windows, no attraction goals, and plenty of snack/diaper margin.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Check ferry status in the morning and call Gros Morne lodging if arrival will be late.
dailyItinerary.why: This is the price of including both Fogo and Gros Morne; the reward is ending with Newfoundland's most dramatic mountain-and-fjord landscape.
moments: Use ferry time as reset time.
Break the drive before the afternoon gets brittle.
Arrive and stay put for three nights.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Transport includes fuel, ferry, and rental allocation for the longest travel day.

dailyItinerary.title: Tablelands and Woody Point

gallery.alt: Gros Morne mountain and water scenery.
gallery.caption: Gros Morne base day

gallery.alt: Gros Morne lake and mountain scenery.
gallery.caption: Bonne Bay and west-coast feel

dailyItinerary.transport: Norris Point/Rocky Harbour to Tablelands and Woody Point, roughly 45-60 minutes each way depending base.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Tablelands short trail or viewpoint, Discovery Centre, Woody Point harbor, and a relaxed dinner.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If weather is poor, use the Discovery Centre, cafes, and local drives around Bonne Bay.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Inn breakfast, Woody Point lunch, dinner at the inn or Rocky Harbour.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Carrier for Tablelands; stroller may work only on limited hard-packed sections.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Check Parks Canada programming and road conditions; reserve dinner if needed.
dailyItinerary.why: The Tablelands are the most otherworldly inland landscape in Newfoundland and the best non-boat Gros Morne anchor for a family.
moments: Orange mantle rock below green mountains.
Woody Point village and Bonne Bay views.
Indoor Discovery Centre backup.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Small park/museum costs; no high-cost activity required.

dailyItinerary.title: Western Brook Pond or Green Gardens decision

gallery.alt: Gros Morne scenic water and hills.
gallery.caption: Land-based backup still looks like this

dailyItinerary.transport: Western Brook Pond parking is about 45-60 minutes from Rocky Harbour/Norris Point; boat access requires a flat approach walk.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Western Brook Pond boat tour if baby and weather align; otherwise do Green Point, Lobster Cove Head, or the first safe stretch of Green Gardens.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: Skip the boat and keep the day to lighthouse, beach, and short viewpoints.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Early breakfast, packed lunch or boat-day snacks, final Gros Morne dinner.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Boat requires a carrier and tolerance for the approach walk; choose the land-only backup if wind, rain, or nap timing is off.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Reserve BonTours/Western Brook only after checking infant policy, approach walk, and cancellation rules.
dailyItinerary.why: Western Brook Pond is the signature postcard day, but the plan keeps a strong land-based alternative so the final full day does not depend on a boat.
moments: Fjord-like cliffs if the boat works.
Lighthouse and beach backup if it does not.
Pack slowly before departure day.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Activity assumes two adult boat tickets. Land-only version saves most of this cost.

dailyItinerary.title: Fly Deer Lake to ATL

gallery.alt: Western Brook Pond and Gros Morne scenery.
gallery.caption: Last look at Gros Morne
The trip ends after the big view
A colorful bookend to the route

dailyItinerary.transport: Drive about 1-1.25 hours to Deer Lake Airport, return car, and fly YDF to ATL via Toronto or best available connection.
dailyItinerary.primaryActivity: Departure day only; no sightseeing target unless flight time is late and everyone is rested.
dailyItinerary.backupActivity: If Deer Lake pricing or timing fails, add a final night near Deer Lake or rework to return from St. John's.
dailyItinerary.foodPlan: Breakfast at lodging, airport/connection food, home dinner if timing works.
dailyItinerary.babyPlan: Leave a large airport buffer; rural-road delays and car-seat logistics are the enemy.
dailyItinerary.bookingPriority: Choose a departure that does not require a pre-dawn drive from Gros Morne.
dailyItinerary.why: Flying from Deer Lake preserves the Gros Morne finale and avoids wasting the last full day on a cross-island reposition.
moments: Short final drive compared with returning to St. John's.
One-car rental return at YDF if priced reasonably.
Return flights already counted in Day 1.
dailyItinerary.costNote: Return flight is included in Day 1's flight budget; this day covers local departure costs only.
